1.explanation: The collapse‐toggle behavior is defined in ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js. Its hideEmptyLabels helper only hides labels with no businessObject.name, and it’s only invoked when expanding a subprocess – never when collapsing. As a result, labeled children remain visible (and then appear outside the new collapsed bounds). Fixing the issue requires changing ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js to hide all embedded labels on collapse (regardless of name) and invoke that hiding logic in the collapse branch of the handler.
1.bug_scenario: When you draw a BPMN subprocess, expand it, place a start event, a task and an end event inside, give each a label, then collapse the subprocess via the toggle button, the labels of the embedded elements remain visible (and the start‐event’s label even leaps far outside the now small collapsed box). By contrast the expected behavior is that all labels on elements inside a collapsed subprocess should be hidden.
